title: What Sawa Checks Before an Operator Can List
excerpt: Sawa checks a Ministry licence, ETAA registration, insurance and a track record before any agency can sell seats or operate a departure. See the checklist.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Before an agency can sell seats or operate a departure on Sawa, it must show three things: a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration and passenger and liability insurance, plus a track record of two references or a portfolio. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry, in a review that usually takes two to four business days. The licence and the ETAA registration can also be checked by the public through the Ministry and the ETAA companies index, so the review mirrors what a traveller can verify. No documents, no place on the platform.

The Egyptian Travel Agents Association provides an independent place to check agency membership.

Key facts

Fact Detail
Who is checked Every agency that applies, whether it wants to sell seats, operate departures or both
Check 1 Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence
Check 2 ETAA registration (the Egyptian Travel Agents Association)
Check 3 Passenger and liability insurance
Track record Two references, or a portfolio with review links
How the public can check The Ministry for the licence; the ETAA companies index at etaa-egypt.org for registration
First review Usually two to four business days
Cost to join None. Sawa takes 10% of the selling price
What travellers see The operating agency, named before the deposit is due
Group size Four travellers confirm a date; eight at most
Where to look Partners · Apply and verify · How it works

Every Sawa departure is run by a company most travellers have never heard of. That is by design: the platform connects travellers with real Egyptian agencies, not with a brand that owns every bus. It puts weight on one question: who checked that this company is real? This guide names the checklist, explains how each check works and shows how anyone can run the same checks. It comes from the people behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure marketplace, where the founder has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993.

How does Sawa vet its tour operators?

Sawa vets agencies with a document check: a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration, passenger and liability insurance and a track record, reviewed before an agency can sell a seat or operate a departure. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry.

The check applies to every agency without exception, and the rule behind it is one sentence: no documents, no place on the platform. The licence and the ETAA registration are the ones the public can verify independently. Sawa is a marketplace operated by Online Era (registration 148500). It does not run tours itself. The agency that does is licensed, registered and insured, which is why the vetting exists.

The checklist: the three documents

The check What Sawa looks at How anyone can check it What it protects against
Tourism licence The company's Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, valid and in the company's name Through the Ministry; see the guide on checking a company's licence Unlicensed operators
ETAA registration The company's registration with the Egyptian Travel Agents Association The ETAA companies index at etaa-egypt.org, searched by the company's legal name Companies with no standing in the industry
Insurance Passenger and liability insurance Ask Sawa; insurance is part of the review Trips with no cover behind them
Track record Two references, or a portfolio with review links Reviews the agency publishes itself Companies with no history of running tours

The mirror is the point. What Sawa checks before an agency joins is what the public can check afterwards, so nothing in the vetting is hidden from the people it protects.

The review window

The first review usually takes two to four business days. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry. A missing or expired document delays the application until it is put right, so a gap costs days, not the application. After approval comes an onboarding call, then the agency goes live. The steps are on the apply and verify page.

Newer agencies are welcome but must show references or a portfolio.

What this means for operators

For an agency, the checklist works in both directions. It protects you from being undercut by unlicensed operators, and it gives travellers a reason to trust a departure run by a company they have never heard of.

  • Your licence and registration are public. Travellers can look up the company by its legal name, so use the same legal name everywhere.
  • Your name reaches the traveller. When you operate a departure, your company is named to its travellers before the deposit is due.
  • Your documents must stay current. Your licence, ETAA registration and insurance are the basis of your place on the platform, so renew them before they lapse.

The three questions worth asking before any booking, on Sawa or elsewhere, fall out of the same checklist: which licensed company runs this departure, what is its licence, and what are the cancellation terms. On Sawa, a day tour cancelled more than 48 hours before departure is a full refund, deposit included; less than 48 hours means the 10% deposit is retained; force majeure is a full refund. Packages and cruises have longer terms: no charge 30 or more days out, half the deposit (12.5%) from 29 to 15 days, and the deposit (25%) retained at 14 days or fewer. The details are in the terms. The trust picture around the platform itself is in Is Sawa Tours legit?.

Who vets, who runs, who pays

The structure has three roles, kept separate on purpose.

  • Sawa (operated by Online Era, registration 148500) vets the agencies, owns the catalogue, calendar and prices, and confirms dates at the GoAhead, when four travellers have reserved. Traveller payments go through a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros.
  • The operating agency is one of the licensed agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. It runs the tour under its own licence, with a licensed guide, and earns its operating costs plus an agreed fee, plus the pool share on seats it sold itself.
  • Selling agencies sell seats and earn a share of the pool for each seat, paid as set in the agency agreement.

Travellers reserve free, pay nothing until the date confirms, and travel in a group of eight at most. The mechanics are on how it works, and the agencies that have passed the review are on the partners page.

The short version

Sawa checks every agency before it joins: a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration, insurance and a track record, reviewed in usually two to four business days. The licence and the registration can be checked by anyone, so a traveller can verify the company named on a departure before paying anything, which on Sawa is only ever after four travellers confirm the date. To join yourself, see sawa.tours/operators.

About the author

Islam Hussein is an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, and the founder of Sawa Tours. More about Sawa Tours.

faq.q: How does Sawa vet its tour operators?
faq.a: It checks three documents before an agency can sell seats or operate a departure: a Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities licence, ETAA registration and passenger and liability insurance, plus a track record of references or a portfolio. We check the documents and confirm the licence with the Ministry; the review usually takes two to four business days. No documents, no place on the platform.

faq.q: Can an unlicensed operator join Sawa?
faq.a: No. The Ministry licence and the ETAA registration are the bar. An agency without both cannot be approved, and the operating agency is named to travellers before the deposit is due, so anyone can check it before any money moves.

faq.q: Do selling agencies need the same documents?
faq.a: Yes. An agency needs all three documents whether it wants to sell seats, operate departures or both.

faq.q: How can I verify the operator on my departure myself?
faq.a: Take the operating agency's legal name, which you are given before the deposit is due, search for it in the ETAA companies index at etaa-egypt.org, and check its licence with the Ministry. The walkthrough is in our licence-checking guide .

faq.q: Where can I see the agencies that have passed?
faq.a: On the partners page , which links to each partner's entry on the ETAA register.
